links.outcome: Emergency arrhythmia detection and overcalling by multimodal LLMs on pediatric ECGs
links.effect: Gemini had 100% sensitivity (95% CI 85.1-100.0) for emergency abnormality, -LR 0.07, in n=22, but specificity 30.2% and +LR 1.40, indicating overcalling (unnecessary escalation).
links.quote: For the emergency endpoint, Gemini achieved 100% sensitivity (95% CI = 85.1-100.0) with - LR 0.07 (95% CI = 0.00-1.12) in a small subgroup (n = 22); however, specificity of 30.2% and + LR of 1.40 indicate overcalling rather than diagnostic precision.

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance of LLMs on prospectively collected real pediatric ECGs
links.effect: AUC ranged from 0.550 to 0.623 (modest discrimination); +LR 2.05, 1.26, 1.21 and -LR 0.68, 0.55, 0.81 for clinically significant abnormality; no model achieved meaningful rule-in utility.
links.quote: No model achieved clinically meaningful rule-in utility for either endpoint.

links.outcome: Suitability of multimodal LLM outputs as standalone diagnosis of pediatric ECG
links.effect: +LR values near 1.0 across both endpoints; authors conclude standalone deployment is not supported and tools may only serve as adjunctive screening aids under clinician oversight.
links.quote: Standalone deployment is not supported; these tools may at most serve as adjunctive screening aids under clinician oversight.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility of commercial multimodal LLMs for interpreting pediatric ECGs against cardiologist reference standards, but tests model performance rather than evaluating an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
